stories.headline: Feature spotlight: the Operator's shadow-casting flashlight
stories.summary: A retrospective look at CUSTODIAN's existing Operator flashlight: a directional warm beam casts shadows while a softer local glow helps nearby visibility. The Godot implementation and smoke-test source exist; this is not a new launch or an independently verified runtime demo.
stories.body: This is a retrospective spotlight on an existing Godot component, inspected November 11, 2026. The Operator carries an aim-directed flashlight that starts off and toggles using the configured input. A warm, shadow-casting PointLight2D beam and an unshadowed nearby glow serve separate visual roles. The design documents the Undergate Mechanism Hall as the first flashlight-dominant environment. Source and smoke-test scripts are present; this report has not run Godot or captured in-game proof.
bullets: Existing scene/script are present on main; this is historical coverage, not a new release.
Directional shadows and near-field glow have separate visual purposes.
The published test script checks aim, toggle, and component composition; a fresh run is not claimed.
A fresh Godot smoke result and an in-game capture would show runtime behavior.

article.lead: An archive spotlight, not breaking news: CUSTODIAN already has a flashlight component for its Operator. The warm, aim-directed beam casts shadows, while a second, softer glow helps reveal nearby space. The actual Godot scene, script, and test source were inspected on November 11, 2026; this feature's original release date is not established here.

sections.heading: Two jobs for one flashlight
sections.text: The scene combines a focused shadow-casting beam with a broad, unshadowed glow. This preserves meaningful darkness and geometry while keeping the Operator's immediate surroundings legible.

sections.heading: Equipment without busywork
sections.text: The flashlight is permanent equipment. It starts off, toggles on demand, and follows the Operator's existing aim vector. When the aim briefly becomes zero, the beam holds its last valid facing. The current design intentionally avoids battery, durability, loot, and upgrade systems.

sections.heading: Built for authored darkness
sections.text: Design notes name the Undergate Mechanism Hall as a flashlight-dominant environment with machinery occluders and selective light pools. That's an authored vision supported by source files, not proof of a newly played or captured build.

insights.title: Exploration becomes a lighting problem
insights.explanation: A beam that actually casts shadows invites authored machinery, occlusion, and local light to participate in how a space is explored.

insights.title: A single aim source keeps controls coherent
insights.explanation: The flashlight follows the Operator's own aim direction rather than maintaining a competing input system, and keeps its orientation through brief zero-input moments.

article.takeaway: The flashlight is implemented in source with distinct shadow and glow behavior. No fresh runtime validation or visual demonstration is claimed.
article.next_watch: A recorded Godot smoke run and a public, verified in-game image of the Undergate Mechanism Hall would establish the next level of evidence.

article.lead: A newly documented repair targets a subtle review-history problem that can stall CUSTODIAN's art pipeline. When an archived review packet is restored later, its identical contents can appear to have two creation points. A proposed resolver change would use the actual Git lifecycle to distinguish the original from the restoration.

sections.heading: Why this matters for asset intake
sections.text: The Ash-Bell Surface Lift asset-intake review depends on a trustworthy historical target. Picking a later restored copy could attach independent-review evidence to the wrong implementation; refusing every duplicate history can leave valid work stranded.

sections.heading: A narrow repair, not a shortcut
sections.text: The new P0 manual draft packet specifies ancestry checks: the authentic archive introduction must follow a matching active packet and have a demonstrable retirement. Histories that do not prove a unique candidate must still fail closed. A separate fresh reviewer must test the landed code before the Lift review resumes.

insights.title: Identical bytes do not establish historical identity
insights.explanation: The proposed change distinguishes content equality from the actual lifecycle of a review packet, reducing both false attribution and unnecessary ambiguity.

insights.title: The art pipeline is waiting on review integrity
insights.explanation: Ash-Bell intake remains held not because new art is necessarily defective, but because its review target must be established reliably before acceptance.

article.takeaway: Two draft packets establish a specific repair and independent-review plan; they do not establish that the resolver is fixed.
article.next_watch: Look for a landed resolver implementation with adversarial tests, followed by a genuine independent passing receipt before the preserved Ash-Bell review resumes.

stories.summary: A new main-branch documentation commit clarifies that V2 claim and claim-next perform their own source and safety checks. Legacy audit lock/dependency classifications remain diagnostic, not acquisition authority. A separate explicit human hold still protects the Weather provenance bridge while Operator Chassis review remains unresolved.
stories.body: Main 8262ac57622059256f9f5d136ef0eff28dd59a1d updates AGENTS guidance, lifecycle documentation and Weather source-provenance packets. V2 claim/claim-next authenticate fetched origin/main packet bytes and apply V2 hold, source, checkout, storage, LFS and provenance checks; legacy audit/status classifications do not determine V2 eligibility. Paired-review runner retains separate review gates. The Weather provenance bridge has an explicit orchestration hold external to automatic V2 eligibility until the Operator Chassis review is resolved and the hold is lifted. This is a documentation correction, not evidence that any claim was made, review accepted, or host state changed. Private WIRE pilot pointer remains dated November 8; no new operational counts are promoted. Combined statuses and PR-triggered runs for this commit returned none; CI health is unknown.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN has corrected an important ambiguity in how its task dispatcher is described. A legacy queue audit can label work blocked by dependencies or locks, but those labels are not what authorizes a V2 task claim. The change clarifies authority without releasing any existing hold.

sections.heading: Two views of the queue, only one acquisition path
sections.text: The current V2 claim commands authenticate task identity and packet bytes against fetched main, then enforce their own source, hold, checkout and provenance checks. Legacy audit and status reports remain useful diagnostics, but cannot approve or veto a V2 claim.

sections.heading: An explicit hold still protects the Weather bridge
sections.text: The Weather source-provenance bridge is under a documented human orchestration hold while the separate Operator Chassis review remains unresolved. The correction does not lift that hold or disturb the preserved claim, run or branch. Paired reviews retain their own acceptance gates.

insights.title: A blocked audit label is not the final authority
insights.explanation: The documentation now distinguishes historical queue classifications from the actual V2 acquisition checks, reducing the risk of false claims about eligibility.

insights.title: Human coordination remains decisive
insights.explanation: Even if the V2 command could technically acquire a packet, the explicit Weather bridge hold still prohibits that action until orchestration lifts it.

article.takeaway: This is an important correction to operational guidance, not a new execution or accepted review.
article.next_watch: Watch for a verified Operator Chassis review disposition and explicit lifting of the Weather bridge orchestration hold.

stories.headline: Findings recovery bridge merges; implementation closeout lands while independent review remains ahead
stories.summary: PR #133 merged the exact-run findings recovery bridge into main, and PR #134 landed its implementation closeout. The bridge preserves original nonpassing R0-01/R0-02 findings and requires digest-bound evidence. Passing checks and archived implementation do not establish independent review acceptance, recovery application, or teardown.
stories.body: Main 6ce61c8f8b101d88e8c05f0312cd1f4931873743 includes PR #133 merge e311c9c6417cf4f403bd2586dcf6449a87743dbd and PR #134 closeout. The new code provides a read-only exact-run findings recovery plan and digest-bound apply mechanism restricted to a separate recovery checkout. The implementation closeout reports 326 paired-review runner tests, 14 artifact tests, and 13 synthetic bridge cases passing, plus changed-file checks. Those checks do not constitute a fresh independent PASS. The designated independent review review-agent-paired-review-findings-artifact-recovery-v1 remains the next gate; no recovery apply or canonical host teardown was independently verified. Private pilot pointer is dated November 8, so no operational counts are promoted. CI combined-status endpoint returned no statuses; broader CI health is unknown.

article.lead: A recovery tool for stranded reviewer findings has moved from an assignment into an open pull request. It aims to preserve what the reviewer actually found, without rewriting the original review or pretending the findings were an approval.

sections.heading: A safer route to an authentic record
sections.text: The proposed bridge separates read-only planning from a digest-bound application step. It is tied to one preserved review run and keeps the original checkout and reviewed implementation unchanged. The original R0-01 and R0-02 findings remain findings, not a passing review.
